The test image is a microscopic view (20 µm scale) of a fungal spore chain — multicellular conidia with muriform (brick-like) septation and a beaked apical tip. This is not a typical plant part image but rather a pathogen spore morphology image.

Key features:
- Chain of 2-3 multicellular conidia
- Both transverse and longitudinal septa (muriform)
- Beaked/elongated terminal cell
- Pale olive/cream color
- ~20 µm scale

The Alternaria description explicitly mentions: "hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell on the terminal end, 7-18 x 18-50 µm." This matches closely. Now viewing one reference from each of my top 4 candidates.
Strong match — the Alternaria reference shows chains of multicellular conidia with the same beaked, septate structure visible in the test image. Now checking 3 more classes.
Anthracnose shows macroscopic acervuli with setae on stem tissue — completely different from the microscopic spore chain in the test image. Now checking Septoria and Gray Mold.
Septoria shows macroscopic leaf spots — no match to the microscopic spore image. Now checking Gray Mold.

Gray Mold (Botrytis) shows clusters of small round unicellular conidia on branching conidiophores — completely different from the large muriform chain conidia in the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**

| Class | Match |
|---|---|
| Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers | Strong — reference shows same multicellular beaked conidia in chains |
| Anthracnose | No — macroscopic acervuli with setae |
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | No — macroscopic leaf spots |
| Gray_Mold | No — small round unicellular conidia in grape-like clusters |

The test image is a microscopic photo (20 µm scale bar) of **Alternaria conidia**: large muriform (multi-septate in both planes), club-shaped, in a chain of 2-3, with a distinct beaked terminal cell. This exactly matches the KB description: *"hand grenade-shaped with a shorter beaked apical cell on the terminal end, 7-18 x 18-50 µm."* The Alternaria reference image (Bugwood_13) confirms this morphology with nearly identical conidial chains.
